title: Surge stitching bug caused prolonged coldstarts and customer escalations
creator: Asha Patel
description: On 2026-03-10 we received multiple customer escalations (ACME Health, ShopRight) reporting sustained coldstarts and elevated latencies for burst traffic on Dedicated capacity. The root cause was a bug in the "surge-stitcher" component of the autoscaler that combines per-allocator headroom signals across heterogeneous GPU pools. The bug caused much of the computed headroom to be truncated when the quantile-smoothing path encountered an unexpected zero-padding edge case for small tenants, resulting in effective headroom underreporting and failure to trigger timely scale-ups. This ticket tracked the triage, mitigation, hotfix, rollout, and postmortem actions.
root_cause: surge-stitcher quantile-smoothing truncated fractional headroom for small tenants due to zero-padding branch + integer conversion path. Combined with a tenant-affinity heuristic that preferred cold pools, requests were routed to under-provisioned pools and burst credits were double-applied during reconciliation, causing sustained underprovisioning and coldstarts.
impact_summary: A subset of Dedicated tenants experienced token-level latency spikes (p99 increase from ~120ms to ~1.2s) and request queuing for bursts lasting 30-90 minutes. ~12 paying customers reported user-visible errors; two customers escalated to enterprise support. Traffic patterns resembling short microbursts (20–200 concurrent requests over 2–8s) were most affected.
mitigation_steps: 2026-03-10 13:12 UTC: Opened incident, notified on-call, escalated to platform lead
2026-03-10 13:40 UTC: Emergency policy — manual inject of +12 reserved GPUs into rsv-pool-45 to buy headroom for affected tenants
2026-03-10 14:05 UTC: Temporarily disabled quantile-smoothing heuristic on surge-stitcher via feature flag to restore conservative headroom aggregation
2026-03-10 14:30 UTC: Created emergency fallback routing rule to prefer warm pools for tenants with recent burst history
2026-03-10 16:00 UTC: Customer comms sent: initial incident advisory and mitigation steps; triage notes shared with ACME Health and ShopRight
fix_description: Implemented a hotfix that (1) fixes the zero-padding edge path and preserves fractional headroom by switching aggregation to a float64 accumulator, (2) adds explicit safeguards against double-counting burst credits in the reconciler, and (3) tightens tenant-affinity scoring to prefer warm pools when recent burst history exists. Added unit and integration tests for heterogeneous GPU workflows and a regression test for microburst patterns.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout: 10% of surge-stitcher pods in us-west-2 (2026-03-11 02:00 UTC)
Scale to 50% after 1 hour of stable telemetry (2026-03-11 03:15 UTC)
Full rollout across regions after 4 hours of acceptable headroom metrics (2026-03-11 06:30 UTC)
Feature-flag revert path tested: rollback in <5 minutes via console if regressions observed
monitoring_and_metrics_changes: Added alert: aggregated_headroom_fraction < 0.2 for 2m across >3 pools tagged 'dedicated'
Added reconciliation audit logs for burst-credit adjustments (retained 90d)
Dashboard: Dedicated > Autoscaler > Surge stitching overview (link below)
postmortem_actions: Add end-to-end chaos test for microburst patterns in the CI scale harness (owner: infra-testing)
Add synthetic load job that replays affected tenant burst traces nightly and validates headroom signals (owner: serving-runtime)
Audit other aggregation paths for similar integer/float truncation issues (owner: scheduler)
Schedule runbook update: include manual GPU injection and feature-flag checklist (owner: oncall-playbooks)
Customer follow-up: 1:1 postmortem with ACME Health and ShopRight; offer credits as appropriate (owner: CSMs)
Ship telemetry rollup in runtime-1.25 with retention and export to long-term metrics store (owner: observability)
